name: Application Security (SAST, DAST, Secrets & SCA)
tagline: Product-security gates for the code and recipes you ship: SAST, DAST, secrets detection, dependency (SCA), fuzzing, and threat modeling — nested by technique for dev and DevProd teams.

tools.name: Semgrep
tools.desc: Lightweight app-sec static analyzer for 30+ languages: YAML rules that read like the code they match, bundled security packs (p/security-audit, p/owasp-top-ten), and pre-commit/CI/IDE hooks.
tools.when: The default SAST layer for any dev team: run it per-PR in CI or in the editor to catch injection, dangerous-API misuse, and hardcoded secrets before merge.

tools.name: CodeQL
tools.desc: GitHub's query-based analysis engine that databases your code and runs QL queries to find vulnerability classes; the CLI is free and the strongest maintained rule sets ship through GitHub code scanning.
tools.when: High-signal coverage on GitHub-hosted repos: enable code scanning on schedules and PRs, then drop into the CodeQL CLI to run or author bespoke queries on a local database.
tools.install: Download the CodeQL CLI bundle from github.com/github/codeql-action/releases

tools.name: SonarQube
tools.desc: Self-hosted code-quality and security platform: the Community Edition runs hundreds of static rules over 30+ languages with dashboards, quality gates, and trended security reports.
tools.when: When an org needs a shared, dashboard-visible quality gate and SAST history instead of per-commit CLI output.

tools.name: Bandit
tools.desc: PyCQA's AST-based Python analyzer flags common first-party mistakes — SQLi, shell injection, pickles, eval, weak crypto, and path permissions — with a low-noise report you can tune.
tools.when: A no-config SAST pass for Python services: pip-install, point it at the package directory, and wire into CI.

tools.name: gosec
tools.desc: SecureGo's Go static analyzer walking ASTs and data flow to find hardcoded creds, weak TLS configs, unsafe sql/exec sinks, and integer-overflow risk in first-party Go code.
tools.when: The quick Go-specific SAST gate in CI, alongside or before a language-agnostic scanner like Semgrep.

tools.name: Brakeman
tools.desc: The reference Ruby on Rails scanner: static analysis tuned to Rails patterns (SQL injection, XSS, mass assignment, unsafe deserialization) with actionable remediation notes.
tools.when: Any Rails/Ruby codebase in CI: one command and the framework-aware findings are worth more than generic engines.

tools.name: SpotBugs + FindSecBugs
tools.desc: SpotBugs is the Java bytecode static analyzer; the FindSecBugs plugin adds 120+ security patterns (path traversal, XXE, weak crypto, injection sinks) to its findings.
tools.when: Java/JVM builds that need bytecode-level findings beyond a pattern scanner — wire the Maven/Gradle plugin into the build.

tools.name: Security Code Scan (.NET)
tools.desc: An open-source Roslyn analyzer that adds taint-tracking security rules for C#: SQL injection, deserialization, path traversal, and cryptographically weak constructs.
tools.when: .NET solutions in CI: install the NuGet analyzer and let it run inline with the build for zero extra infra.

tools.name: eslint-plugin-security
tools.desc: Node.js Security's ESLint plugin that flags hardcoded credentials, unsafe regex, non-literal require/child_process, and other JS security smells directly in lint output.
tools.when: Node/JS repos already on ESLint: enable the security ruleset for the fastest in-editor security feedback.

tools.name: Psalm
tools.desc: PHP static analysis with a taint-check mode (`--taint-analysis`) that traces untrusted input to sinks for SQLi, XSS, file access, and more.
tools.when: PHP projects wanting first-party vulnerability detection in CI without a managed SaaS.

tools.name: viperstrike
tools.desc: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server vulnerability auditor — AST/whitebox SAST for agentic AI tool handlers, SARIF-capable, optional oracle runtime mode.
tools.when: Auditing MCP servers and AI tool endpoints for handler-level vulnerabilities.

tools.name: OWASP ZAP
tools.desc: Full web/API security scanner: intercepting proxy, spider, passive + active scanning, and a programmable REST API; ships zap-baseline.py and Docker images ready for automated CI DAST.
tools.when: Stand up per-app DAST: run the baseline scan against a staging build nightly or per-PR, then use the proxy for manual testing of tricky auth flows.

tools.name: Nuclei
tools.desc: ProjectDiscovery's template-driven vulnerability scanner with 8,000+ community YAML templates (CVEs, exposures, misconfigs) and fast protocol-level scanning.
tools.when: Broad templated coverage across an app inventory — feed it URLs/HTTP inputs in CI and get CVE-check results without bespoke rules.

tools.name: Wapiti
tools.desc: Python black-box web scanner performing GET/POST parameter fuzzing for OWASP classes (SQLi, XSS, file inclusion, command injection) with a DAST REST API.
tools.when: Scriptable scan of internal apps where you want a ZAP alternative with no Docker dependency and easy output automation.

tools.name: Burp Suite
tools.desc: PortSwigger's leading web application testing platform: Community gives the intercepting proxy, history, and Repeater/Decoder manual tools free; the automated scanner is paid.
tools.when: Manual pentest-style review of your own apps: drive the app through the proxy, then replay, tamper, and fuzz individual requests by hand.

tools.name: Arachni
tools.desc: Ruby-based web scanner with a rich modular architecture and REST/WebSocket APIs; unmaintained for several years but deployable standalone or embedded.
tools.when: Legacy stacks that ship its browser-based grid, or when you want its fingerprinting modules self-hosted — otherwise prefer ZAP or Nuclei.

tools.name: RESTler
tools.desc: Microsoft's stateful REST API fuzzer: ingests your OpenAPI spec, infers producer-consumer request dependencies, then fuzzes request sequences to surface 5xx crashes, resource leaks, and security-checker violations.
tools.when: API-only DAST beyond the HTML UI: after a ZAP baseline, point RESTler at the schema to grind through every endpoint and parameter combination.
tools.install: Download the RESTler release archive from github.com/microsoft/restler-fuzzer/releases

tools.name: Schemathesis
tools.desc: Property-based API testing against OpenAPI/GraphQL schemas: generates edge-case and adversarial requests and can run its built-in security checks against each response.
tools.when: Shift-left API testing in CI where you want schema-driven request generation plus explicit security assertions, with a GiHub Action.

tools.name: OWASP Dependency-Check
tools.desc: OWASP's SCA utility that fingerprints declared dependencies (Java, .NET, Python, Node, Ruby, Go, Rust, and more) against NVD and other feeds, emitting CVSS-scored known-CVE reports.
tools.when: The reference dependency gate for build output: run on release builds to block known-vulnerable libraries before they ship; the first run downloads the full NVD feed.

tools.name: OSV-Scanner
tools.desc: Google's open-source vulnerability scanner (the engine behind GitHub Dependabot) that matches lockfiles and SBOMs against the OSV.dev database — fast, quiet, and free of NVD feed friction.
tools.when: Snappy per-lockfile check in CI (package-lock.json, go.sum, requirements, poetry, etc.) when you want OSV-only coverage without a heavyweight feed.

tools.name: pip-audit
tools.desc: Python Packaging Authority's scanner audits direct and transitive PyPI requirements against OSV/advisory feeds, and can auto-fix vulnerable packages installed locally (--fix).
tools.when: Python-only repos: the smallest honest way to keep requirements.txt/pyproject dependency lists clean as part of pre-commit or CI.

tools.name: npm audit
tools.desc: Bundled npm command that checks the installed dependency tree against the npm advisory database and can auto-downgrade (`npm audit fix`) where a patched version exists.
tools.when: Zero-setup Node dependency gate: run in CI after install and block on high/critical findings.
tools.install: Bundled with npm — no install needed

tools.name: govulncheck
tools.desc: The Go team's vulnerability scanner: uses static analysis of function call graphs to report only findings that are actually reachable from your code, not every transitive dependency.
tools.when: Go modules in CI: `govulncheck ./...` gives call-reachable CVEs with far less noise than generic SCA.

tools.name: cargo-audit
tools.desc: RustSec's lockfile auditor (cargo.lock) reporting known vulnerabilities from the RustSec Advisory Database, with `cargo audit fix` for auto-updates.
tools.when: Rust projects in CI: run against the committed Cargo.lock every PR.

tools.name: Grype + Syft
tools.desc: Anchore's pair: Syft generates SPDX/CycloneDX SBOMs from images and filesystems, Grype matches them against multiple vulnerability feeds with reachability-aware reporting in some modes.
tools.when: Container-first SCA inside the build: generate the SBOM, scan it with Grype, and attach it as a build attestation.

tools.name: Gitleaks
tools.desc: Fastest OSS secret scanner: a single Go binary that sweeps full git history or plain directories with 200+ regex rules for API keys, tokens, and passwords, exporting JSON/SARIF with pre-commit and GitHub Action hooks.
tools.when: Gate every repo and pipeline: full-history sweep when onboarding, then pre-commit/PR scans from then on; the default before anything heavier.

tools.name: TruffleHog
tools.desc: Secret scanner with 600+ credential detectors that actively verify matches against vendor APIs to separate live credentials from noise; scans git, GitHub/GitLab orgs, S3, Docker, and filesystems.
tools.when: Org-wide sweeps where knowing which leaked credentials still work matters more than raw match counts.

tools.name: detect-secrets
tools.desc: Yelp's Python scanner that audits a repo once into a .secrets.baseline then diffs only new lines in pre-commit/CI, so only genuinely new secrets get flagged instead of the same approved ones on every run.
tools.when: Teams worn out by re-flagged false positives: do the one-time audit + baseline review, then let it police new commits.

tools.name: ggshield
tools.desc: GitGuardian's open-source CLI that scans commits, PRs, and CI output for secrets with pre-commit hooks and does live-verification checks; the hosted dashboard beyond it is commercial.
tools.when: Pre-commit + CI hook coverage when you already use GitGuardian's engine conventions and want its detectors locally.

tools.name: AFL++
tools.desc: The maintained successor of American Fuzzy Lop: coverage-guided in-process fuzzing with QEMU and Frida modes, custom mutators, and calibration for both source and pure-binary targets.
tools.when: Fuzz any C/C++ parser or binary you own: compile with afl-clang-fast, seed a corpus, and let parallel instances grind for crashes and hangs.

tools.name: libFuzzer
tools.desc: Clang's in-process, coverage-guided fuzzing library: link a fuzz target function, enable -fsanitize=fuzzer,address, and get corpus minimization plus sanitizer-detected crashes for free.
tools.when: C/C++ libraries in LLVM builds where in-process fuzzing with ASan/UBSan finds more per second than fork-based engines.

tools.name: Honggfuzz
tools.desc: Google's coverage-guided fuzzer with hardware-based performance counters (Intel PT), persistent mode, and simple configuration; strong on Linux for network and file-parsing targets.
tools.when: When you want hardware-assisted coverage on Linux or a fast standalone alternative to AFL++ for your parsers.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/google/honggfuzz.git && cd honggfuzz && make

tools.name: Jazzer
tools.desc: CodeIntelligence's JVM coverage-guided fuzzer built on libFuzzer: fuzzes Java/Kotlin through a JNI agent with sanitizer-like detection of OOM, stack overflow, and exception-based failures.
tools.when: Grab your @FuzzTest hooks and parse untrusted Java input (JSON, XML, protobuf) to find exceptions, hangs, and memory issues.
tools.install: Download the Jazzer release archive from github.com/CodeIntelligenceTesting/jazzer/releases

tools.name: OSS-Fuzz
tools.desc: Google's open-source continuous fuzzing service for critical OSS: builds your project with sanitizers, runs libFuzzer/AFL++/Honggfuzz at scale, and files issues when new bugs are found.
tools.when: You maintain a widely-used open-source library with a C/C++/Golang/Rust surface and want Google-scale fuzzing with zero infra of your own.
tools.install: Follow google/oss-fuzz quickstart (Docker + build.sh) — no direct install

tools.name: ProFuzzBench
tools.desc: TU Delft's highly-configurable benchmark for stateful protocol fuzzing: 8 real network protocols with reproducible AFLNet/AFL++/libFuzzer harnesses and Docker-based campaigns.
tools.when: Evaluate or compare protocol fuzzers, or learn stateful fuzzing against realistic targets before applying it to your own servers.

tools.name: toxindb
tools.desc: RAG retrieval-time poisoning detector — demand-recency discrimination, canary injection, provenance attestation; fully offline, SARIF+MD reports.
tools.when: Checking your own RAG/vector knowledge bases for poisoned or injected content.

tools.name: OWASP Threat Dragon
tools.desc: OWASP's open-source threat-model tooling for STRIDE/LINDDUN workflows with a browser-based or desktop diagram UI that exports models to JSON for CI review automation.
tools.when: Teams that want a shared, reviewable threat model per service without forcing every engineer to learn a coding DSL.

tools.name: pytm
tools.desc: OWASP's Pythonic framework: define your system as Python objects and generate data-flow diagrams, STRIDE threat lists, and mitigations — diffs cleanly in git and runs in CI.
tools.when: When the threat model must live in the repo and be code-reviewed like any other artifact, or is derived from your IaC definitions.

tools.name: Threagile
tools.desc: Agile threat-modeling toolkit driven by a YAML architecture description: auto-generates STRIDE-based risks, diagrams, and reports via CLI or Kubernetes operator, with a rules engine.
tools.when: Organizations that standardize on YAML-first threat modeling and want automated risk catalogs from the same source of truth.
